municipalities.bachelors_change_pts.plain: How many percentage points the share of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher changed between the 2008-2012 window and the latest window (2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot). A positive number means the share rose.
municipalities.bachelors_change_pts.plain_es: Cuántos puntos porcentuales cambió la proporción de adultos con bachillerato o un grado más alto entre la ventana 2008-2012 y la más reciente (2020-2024 en el corte de datos de 2026-10). Un número positivo significa que la proporción subió.
municipalities.bachelors_change_pts.definition: bachelors_pct in the latest window minus the same share in the 2008-2012 window. The latest window is 2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot. The two shares are rounded to one decimal before they are subtracted. Both use the Census Bureau's American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates: table B15003 for the latest window and table B15002 for 2008-2012.
municipalities.bachelors_change_pts.method: round(share_latest − share_2012, 1). share_latest = B15003 cells 022-025 over cell 001. share_2012 = B15002 cells 015-018 (men) and 032-035 (women) over cell 001. Both tables count the same adults and the same degrees (bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate). The field is empty if either share is missing.
municipalities.bachelors_change_pts.how_to_read: A positive value means a larger share of adults hold a degree than in 2008-2012. It is a difference of shares in points, not a percent change. In the 2026-10 snapshot, all 78 municipalities show a gain. On the Housing page you can choose another base year, and the page then shows a different comparison. This field always compares 2008-2012 with the latest window. To cite it in the 2026-10 snapshot, write 'ACS 5-year estimates, 2020-2024 compared with 2008-2012, tables B15003 and B15002, calculated by Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory'.
caveats: It measures the adults who live in the municipality now compared with those who lived there then. It does not follow the same people, so people who left or arrived change the result.
Both shares are survey estimates with their own margins of error. The municipality file (municipalities.json) carries the estimate only, with no margin.

education.he_inst.plain: How many colleges, universities and technical or vocational schools report to the federal postsecondary survey from each municipality.
education.he_inst.plain_es: Cuántos colegios, universidades y escuelas técnicas o vocacionales informan a la encuesta federal de educación postsecundaria desde cada municipio.
education.he_inst.definition: Institutions in the IPEDS directory for the year, in the municipality of their county code: universities, colleges and technical and vocational schools (beauty, nursing and trade schools among them). The central offices of university systems (IPEDS sector 0) and the directory's records marked "not applicable" (sector -1) are not counted.
education.he_inst.method: education_series.py reads the IPEDS directory for Puerto Rico for each year and counts the institutions in each county code whose sector is above 0. Three system offices in San Juan every year and 13 "not applicable" records in 2020 are left out; none has fall enrollment. Names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers' names and coordinates are dropped as the API is read and are never stored or published.
education.he_inst.how_to_read: Puerto Rico had 152 such institutions in 2010 and 126 in 2024.
caveats: A university with campuses that report separately counts once for each campus; one that reports as a whole counts once, where its main office is.
education.he_inst.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the sum of the 78 municipal values)
education.he_inst.source_detail: Urban Institute Education Data Portal API, college-university/ipeds/directory/{year}?fips=72 (unitid, county_fips, sector, control, level) and ipeds/fall-enrollment/{year}/undergraduate and /graduate (totals: race, sex, attendance, degree-seeking and class level 99)

education.he_enroll.plain: How many students were enrolled in the fall at the colleges and universities of each municipality.
education.he_enroll.plain_es: Cuántos estudiantes estaban matriculados en el otoño en los colegios y universidades de cada municipio.
education.he_enroll.definition: Undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in the fall at the IPEDS institutions of the municipality, full-time and part-time.
education.he_enroll.method: education_series.py adds the undergraduate and graduate fall enrollment totals of each institution to the municipality of its directory row. Names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers' names and coordinates are dropped as the API is read and are never stored or published.
education.he_enroll.how_to_read: College enrollment in Puerto Rico fell from 270,920 in fall 2010 to 171,760 in fall 2024. In 2024 the largest are San Juan 43,670, Bayamón 41,648, Ponce 14,130.
caveats: Students are counted where the institution reports: for a university that reports as a whole, its main office, not the campus they attend.
Online students are counted at their institution, wherever they live.

degrees.deg_associate.plain: How many associate degrees colleges in an area awarded in an academic year.
degrees.deg_associate.plain_es: Cuántos grados asociados otorgaron las universidades de un área en un año académico.
degrees.deg_associate.definition: Associate degrees awarded in the academic year (IPEDS award level 3), first majors only. Counted at the campus that reports to IPEDS, not where the graduates live; a municipio with no college has 0. A college may report all its campuses from one place: NUC University reports its campuses and online programmes from Bayamón. The year is the end of the academic year (2024 = 2023-24).
degrees.deg_associate.method: degrees.py reads NCES's IPEDS completions file and directory for each academic year, keeps Puerto Rico's institutions and first majors only, and adds each institution's awards to the municipio of its campus in that year's directory. Award levels: associate 3, bachelor's 5, master's 7, doctor's 17, 18 and 19. Fields are the first two digits of the CIP code. Two checks run every year: the six-digit rows add up to the file's own total (CIP 99) for every level, and the fields add up to the bachelor's and graduate degrees.
caveats: Counted at the campus that reports to IPEDS, not where graduates live: most municipios have no college and read 0. A college may report all its campuses from one place: NUC University reports its campuses and online programmes from Bayamón (14,321 awards, 29.4% of the island's in 2023-24, mostly certificates), so Bayamón's count is far above where its students study.
Institutions report their own counts to NCES; a year is the academic year that ends in it (2024 = 2023-24).
First majors only: a student with two majors counts once.
degrees.deg_associate.source_detail: NCES IPEDS completions (first majors) and directory, academic years ending 2015 to 2024, read from NCES's complete data files; counted by the municipio of each campus

housing.bachelors_pct.plain: Out of every 100 adults aged 25 or older, how many hold a bachelor's degree or a higher degree (master's, professional or doctorate). Puerto Rico: 29.8% in 2020-2024.
housing.bachelors_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 adultos de 25 años o más, cuántos tienen un bachillerato o un grado más alto (maestría, grado profesional o doctorado). Puerto Rico: 29.8% en 2020-2024.
housing.bachelors_pct.definition: Adults 25 and over whose highest degree is a bachelor's, master's, professional school degree or doctorate (American Community Survey, ACS, table B15002, cells 15-18 for men and 32-35 for women) divided by all adults 25 and over (B15002, cell 1), times 100.
housing.bachelors_pct.method: The observatory reads the table for every window: the per-sequence summary files for 2010-2020 and the table-based summary files for 2021-2024, for the 78 municipio rows and the Puerto Rico row. It adds cells 15, 16, 17, 18, 32, 33, 34 and 35 and divides by cell 1. The margin of error of the share is computed by the observatory from the published margins of its parts, with the Census Bureau's formulas for sums (margins added in quadrature) and for a proportion whose numerator is part of the denominator.
housing.bachelors_pct.how_to_read: A value of 30 means that 30 of every 100 adults aged 25 or older hold at least a bachelor's degree. Associate degrees are not counted. The measure follows where people live now, so it reflects who moves in or out as well as who studied there. The number after the plus-minus sign (±) is the margin of error. At 90% confidence, the true value probably lies within that distance of the estimate.
caveats: Margins of error are missing for most municipalities from the 2021 window on. In the 2026-10 snapshot, they are present for 78 of 78 municipalities in every window up to 2020 but for only 7, 10, 6 and 5 of 78 in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024. In the Census Bureau's files for 2021 to 2024, the adult total (table B15002, cell 1) has the code -555555555 where a margin of error would be, for most municipalities (73 of the 78 municipality rows in the 2024 file). The observatory leaves a share's margin blank when the margin of its denominator is missing. In the 2010 to 2020 files that margin was a number. The estimates themselves are present for every municipality. For these 284 estimates the Housing page cannot flag unreliable values: the absence of a ± or of italics is not evidence of precision, so treat small-municipality values for 2021 to 2024 with the same caution as earlier years. The Census Bureau uses -555555555 as an annotation code in place of a margin of error; its summary-file documentation lists these codes.

Neighboring windows share four of their five years. To judge change, compare windows that do not overlap, for example 2010-2014, 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 (labeled 2014, 2019 and 2024). See the entry on American Community Survey 5-year windows.

Estimates for small municipalities are imprecise. The municipality profile warns for municipalities with fewer than 25,000 residents. The Full data dialog shows in italics any nonzero value whose margin of error is more than 30% of the estimate. Zero values and values with no published margin are not italicized, so an unmarked value is not proof of precision.
The Puerto Rico value is the Census Bureau's own island-level estimate, not an average of the 78 municipalities.

Also published for barrios and census tracts (acs_barrio.json and acs_tract.json), each value with its margin of error where the Census Bureau gives one. Below the municipality the figure is rough. In 2020-2024 the margin of error is above 30% of the estimate (the CSV by area marks such values as less reliable; no map or table draws areas below the municipality yet) for 66% of barrios and 38% of census tracts that have a value. See methods.small_area_estimates.
housing.bachelors_pct.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico; also 901 barrios and 981 census tracts
housing.bachelors_pct.source_detail: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B15002 (Sex by Educational Attainment for the Population 25 Years and Over); windows 2006-2010 to 2020-2024. Files, under https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/: for windows labeled 2021 to 2024, a table-based file such as 2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/acsdt5y2024-b15002.dat; for windows labeled 2010 to 2020, the per-sequence files in {year}/data/5_year_seq_by_state/PuertoRico/All_Geographies_Not_Tracts_Block_Groups/, where {year} is the last year of the window. Definitions follow the Census Bureau's ACS Subject Definitions (2024 edition: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/subject_definitions/2024_ACSSubjectDefinitions.pdf; each earlier year has its own edition).

municipalities.bachelors_pct.plain: The share of adults aged 25 or older with a bachelor's degree (a four-year degree) or a higher degree.
municipalities.bachelors_pct.plain_es: La proporción de adultos de 25 años o más con un bachillerato (un grado de cuatro años) o un grado más alto.
municipalities.bachelors_pct.definition: Adults aged 25 and over whose highest education is a bachelor's, master's, professional school or doctorate degree, divided by all adults aged 25 and over, times 100. From table B15003 (educational attainment for the population 25 years and over; cells 022 to 025 and 001) of the Census Bureau's American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates for the latest window (2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot).
municipalities.bachelors_pct.method: B15003 cells 022, 023, 024 and 025 added, divided by cell 001, times 100, rounded to one decimal (file acsdt5y2024-b15003.dat in the 2026-10 snapshot). The 2008-2012 baseline for bachelors_change_pts uses the older table B15002 (see municipalities.change_method). The Housing page series uses B15002 for every window. In the 2026-10 snapshot it gives the same 2020-2024 values.
municipalities.bachelors_pct.how_to_read: A higher value means more adults hold a four-year degree or more. It describes adults who live in the municipality, whether or not they work there.
caveats: Associate degrees and some college without a degree are not counted.
The municipality file (municipalities.json) carries the estimate only, with no margin.

In the 2026-10 snapshot (2020-2024 window) the Housing page series shows a margin for only 5 municipalities (Culebra, Florida, Las Marías, Maricao, Vieques). For the other 73 the Census Bureau sets the adult population to its own estimate and publishes no margin for it, and the observatory does not calculate a share's margin without it. A missing margin does not mean the figure is exact: the number of degree holders is still a survey estimate.
municipalities.bachelors_pct.source_detail: ACS 5-year 2020-2024, table B15003, cells 022-025 over cell 001

layers.schools.plain: The open public schools on the map, with their students, grades and the hazard areas each one stands in.
layers.schools.definition: public_schools.geojson: one point per open public school of the newest NCES school directory (2024-25) with a published point: name (as NCES writes it, in capitals without accents), municipio, geoid, students, grades, NCES id and hz, the hazard areas the point stands in. 862 schools with 235,819 students.
layers.schools.method: facility_exposure.py reads the NCES Common Core of Data directory through the Urban Institute's Education Data API (no key), keeps the open schools (status open, new, added, changed agency or reopened) that have a point, and tests each point against FEMA's 1% flood area, NOAA's 3 ft sea level rise area and the USGS landslide susceptibility map. The 2D map (facilities.js) and the 3D view (facilities3d.js) draw it with core/facilities.js, which holds its colour, pop-up and note.
layers.schools.how_to_read: Each orange point is an open public school (862 in 2024-25). Its pop-up gives the students and grades and, when it applies, the hazard areas it stands in. The flags say where the building stands, not that harm will come to it.
caveats: Private schools are not in the NCES public school directory.
The point is the one NCES publishes; a school with several buildings has one point.
A school on land the USGS rates highly susceptible to landslides is rare on the map because a building stands on a levelled pad, which the 5 m map rates by its own slope (docs/facility-exposure.md).

population.acs_no_hs_pct.plain: Out of every 100 adults 25 and older, how many did not finish high school (no diploma or equivalent).
population.acs_no_hs_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 adultos de 25 años o más, cuántos no terminaron la escuela superior (sin diploma ni equivalencia).
population.acs_no_hs_pct.definition: Adults 25 and older whose highest schooling is below a high school diploma or its equivalent, divided by all adults 25 and older (table B15002: cells from 'No schooling completed' to '12th grade, no diploma', men and women), in percent.
population.acs_no_hs_pct.method: The observatory reads table B15002 (Sex by Educational Attainment for the Population 25 Years and Over) of the Census Bureau's American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year files, for each of the four five-year windows, and works the value out by adding the sixteen cells below a high school diploma (003 to 010 and 020 to 027) and dividing by the total (001). The Census Bureau does not publish this table for block groups, so there is no block-group value. The same arithmetic makes the value for a municipality, a barrio, a census tract. The margin of error follows the Census Bureau's formulas: the margin of a sum is the square root of the sum of the squares of the margins of its cells, and a share uses the Bureau's proportion formula. A total that the Census Bureau controls to its own estimate has no margin; the observatory gives it a margin of zero, as the Bureau says may be done, so a share of it keeps the margin of its numerator. A cell the Census Bureau leaves empty gives no value, never a zero. A share whose margin works out to zero (a share of exactly 100%, for example) is published without a margin: the proportion formula would give zero, which would read as exact. The Puerto Rico value is the Census Bureau's own island row. The code is small_area.py in the project's repository.
population.acs_no_hs_pct.how_to_read: In 2020-2024, 18.83% of adults 25 and older in Puerto Rico had no high school diploma (margin ±0.22), against 21.64% in 2017-2021.
caveats: The windows share years: the change from one to the next is not a yearly trend.
Bachelor's degree or higher is a separate dataset (housing.bachelors_pct).
population.acs_no_hs_pct.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico; also 901 barrios and 981 census tracts (not published for block groups)
population.acs_no_hs_pct.source_detail: ACS 5-year table table B15002 (Sex by Educational Attainment for the Population 25 Years and Over), table-based summary files, https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/{vintage}/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/ (vintages 2021 to 2024). The cells used are checked against the Census Bureau's own labels, https://api.census.gov/data/{vintage}/acs/acs5/groups/table.json, in every vintage at every build.

layers.libraries.plain: Libraries registered as public libraries in the E-Rate program, on the map, with their name, type and municipio.
layers.libraries.plain_es: Las bibliotecas inscritas como bibliotecas públicas en el programa E-Rate, en el mapa, con su nombre, tipo y municipio.
layers.libraries.definition: libraries.geojson: one point per active public library of USAC's E-Rate list whose point lies within 1 km of the municipio of its address, with name, type (main library, library or branch, library kiosk, bookmobile), municipio and geoid. 1,099 of 1,228 libraries on 2026-11-07.
layers.libraries.method: facilities.py keeps USAC's active Puerto Rico libraries marked public. A library whose point falls more than 1 km outside the municipio of its address (107) or that has no point (21) is counted there but not drawn. Any telephone number written into a name is removed. The 2D map (facilities.js) and the 3D view (facilities3d.js) draw it with core/facilities.js, which holds its file, colour, pop-up and note.
layers.libraries.how_to_read: Switch the layer on in the Map layers tab of the 2D map or the 3D view (Community services, Education and culture: Public libraries). Both views draw the same points, with the same note on what is counted but not drawn and the same pop-up. Click a point for the library's name, type, municipio and source.
caveats: Most entries are community technology centres and community libraries registered as public libraries, not municipal libraries.
USAC's points are entered by the applicants; some are off by a street or more.

facilities.libraries.plain: How many libraries in each municipio are registered as public libraries in the federal E-Rate program, including community technology centres.
facilities.libraries.plain_es: Cuántas bibliotecas de cada municipio están inscritas como bibliotecas públicas en el programa federal E-Rate, incluidos los centros tecnológicos comunitarios.
facilities.libraries.definition: Active libraries in USAC's E-Rate entity list that USAC marks as public libraries, in the municipio of their address (else of their point). In Puerto Rico the list includes community technology centres and other community libraries registered as public libraries, not only municipal libraries.
facilities.libraries.method: facilities.py asks USAC's Socrata API for Puerto Rico entities of type Library and keeps those that are active and public (1,231 on 2026-10-17). The municipio is the address's city or county when it is a municipio's name or a known postal place (Río Piedras is San Juan); 27 libraries are placed by their point and 2 could not be placed.
facilities.libraries.how_to_read: USAC lists 1,228 placed public libraries in Puerto Rico: San Juan 94, Guaynabo 75, Ponce 48. Every municipio has at least one.
caveats: A registration for federal internet discounts, not a census of libraries: a library that never applied is missing and one that closed may still be listed as active.

Most entries are community technology centres, school-community libraries or church-run centres registered as public libraries; the type says only whether USAC marks it a main library, kiosk or bookmobile.
IMLS's Public Libraries Survey, the usual national source, has no Puerto Rico rows.
facilities.libraries.source_detail: USAC open data 7i5i-83qf (E-Rate Supplemental Entity Information), fields entity_number, entity_name, entity_type, status, physical_city, physical_county, public_library, main_branch, bookmobile, kiosk, latitude, longitude

education.sch_teachers.plain: How many classroom teachers worked in the public schools of each municipality, counted as full-time equivalents.
education.sch_teachers.plain_es: Cuántos maestros de salón de clases trabajaban en las escuelas públicas de cada municipio, contados como equivalentes a tiempo completo.
education.sch_teachers.definition: Classroom teachers of the open public schools of the municipality, in full-time equivalents (two half-time teachers count as one), as the schools report them to the Common Core of Data.
education.sch_teachers.method: education_series.py adds the teachers_fte of the operational schools of each county code; a school that reports no count is left out. Names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers' names and coordinates are dropped as the API is read and are never stored or published.
education.sch_teachers.how_to_read: Use it with the students to see how staffing changed; the ratio is education.sch_ptr.
caveats: Teachers who serve several schools are counted where each school reports them.
Specialists without a class of their own can be included in a school's count.
education.sch_teachers.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the sum of the 78 municipal values)
education.sch_teachers.source_detail: Urban Institute Education Data Portal API, schools/ccd/directory/{year}?fips=72: columns ncessch, county_code, school_status, school_type, school_level, enrollment, teachers_fte, charter, virtual

education.sch_closed.plain: How many public schools that were open the year before were no longer open in each municipality.
education.sch_closed.plain_es: Cuántas escuelas públicas que estaban abiertas el año anterior ya no estaban abiertas en cada municipio.
education.sch_closed.definition: Public schools that were operational in the municipality in the previous school year and are not operational in this one (by NCES school id). No value for 2010, the first year read.
education.sch_closed.method: education_series.py compares the operational school ids of each year with those of the year before and counts, in the municipality of the earlier year, the ids that are no longer operational. It also counts how many of them are operational again the next year (notes.closures_reopened_next_year in the file): 0 or 1 a year, so a change of record is rare. Names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers' names and coordinates are dropped as the API is read and are never stored or published.
education.sch_closed.how_to_read: Shows the waves of closures: 162 schools in 2017-18 and 277 in 2018-19 for Puerto Rico.
caveats: A school that NCES gives a new id counts as a closure and an opening.
A merger of two schools shows as one closure.
education.sch_closed.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the sum of the 78 municipal values)
education.sch_closed.source_detail: Urban Institute Education Data Portal API, schools/ccd/directory/{year}?fips=72: columns ncessch, county_code, school_status, school_type, school_level, enrollment, teachers_fte, charter, virtual

education.sch_open.plain: How many public schools were open in each municipality each school year, from the federal school directory.
education.sch_open.plain_es: Cuántas escuelas públicas estaban abiertas en cada municipio cada año escolar, según el directorio federal de escuelas.
education.sch_open.definition: Public schools that the NCES Common Core of Data lists as operational in the school year (status open, new, added, changed agency or reopened), counted in the municipality of the school's county code. Private schools are not in this collection.
education.sch_open.method: education_series.py reads the CCD school directory for Puerto Rico for each school year from 2010 through the Urban Institute's API and counts the schools whose status is operational in each county code (municipio). Names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers' names and coordinates are dropped as the API is read and are never stored or published.
education.sch_open.how_to_read: Use it to follow the number of public schools over time. Puerto Rico had 1,473 open public schools in 2010-11 and 862 in 2024-25; most of the drop came with the closures of 2017 and 2018 (see education.sch_closed).
caveats: Only public schools: the private schools that many students in Puerto Rico attend are not in this collection.
A school is a building with its own NCES id; one that serves two levels counts once.
education.sch_open.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the sum of the 78 municipal values)
education.sch_open.source_detail: Urban Institute Education Data Portal API, schools/ccd/directory/{year}?fips=72: columns ncessch, county_code, school_status, school_type, school_level, enrollment, teachers_fte, charter, virtual

education.sch_enroll.plain: How many students were enrolled in the public schools of each municipality each school year.
education.sch_enroll.plain_es: Cuántos estudiantes estaban matriculados en las escuelas públicas de cada municipio cada año escolar.
education.sch_enroll.definition: The fall enrollment that each open public school reports to the Common Core of Data, added up for the municipality. A school that reports no count is left out; a municipality whose open schools all lack a count has no value.
education.sch_enroll.method: education_series.py adds the enrollment of the operational schools of each county code; negative codes (missing, not applicable, suppressed) are read as no value. Names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers' names and coordinates are dropped as the API is read and are never stored or published.
education.sch_enroll.how_to_read: Public school enrollment in Puerto Rico fell from 473,410 students in 2010-11 to 235,819 in 2024. In 2024 the largest are San Juan 21,154, Bayamón 12,484, Ponce 10,054.
caveats: Counts students where the school is, not where they live.
Private school students are not included, so a fall can partly be a move to private schools.
education.sch_enroll.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the sum of the 78 municipal values)
education.sch_enroll.source_detail: Urban Institute Education Data Portal API, schools/ccd/directory/{year}?fips=72: columns ncessch, county_code, school_status, school_type, school_level, enrollment, teachers_fte, charter, virtual

education.sch_ptr.plain: On average, how many students there were for each full-time teacher in the public schools of each municipality.
education.sch_ptr.plain_es: En promedio, cuántos estudiantes había por cada maestro a tiempo completo en las escuelas públicas de cada municipio.
education.sch_ptr.definition: Students divided by full-time-equivalent teachers, counting only the open schools that report both numbers. The Puerto Rico value is worked out the same way from all such schools.
education.sch_ptr.method: education_series.py adds, for each county code, the students and the teachers of the schools that report both and divides one by the other. Names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers' names and coordinates are dropped as the API is read and are never stored or published.
education.sch_ptr.how_to_read: Lower means more teachers for each student. For Puerto Rico it went from 13.0 in 2010-11 to 9.74 in 2024, because enrollment fell faster than the number of teachers.
caveats: It is not class size.
A municipality with few schools can move a lot from one year to the next.
education.sch_ptr.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the sum of the 78 municipal values)
education.sch_ptr.source_detail: Urban Institute Education Data Portal API, schools/ccd/directory/{year}?fips=72: columns ncessch, county_code, school_status, school_type, school_level, enrollment, teachers_fte, charter, virtual

school_conditions.crdc_nurse_pct.plain: The share of public schools that report any nurse.
school_conditions.crdc_nurse_pct.plain_es: La proporción de escuelas públicas que informan algún enfermero.
school_conditions.crdc_nurse_pct.definition: Schools that report any nurse (full- or part-time), as a share of the schools that report their staff. Puerto Rico's staff items are missing in 2017-18. Public schools that answered the Civil Rights Data Collection, placed in a municipio by the NCES school directory; the share is pooled over the schools that report both figures, never an average of school shares. The year is the school year that starts in it (2021 = 2021-22); 2019-20 was not collected.
school_conditions.crdc_nurse_pct.method: school_conditions.py reads the all-students rows of the Civil Rights Data Collection for Puerto Rico's public schools, places each school in a municipio by its NCES id in the Common Core of Data directory of the same year, and pools: a municipio's share is the sum of its schools' numerators over the sum of their denominators, over the schools that report both. Negative codes (missing, not applicable, suppressed) are no value.
school_conditions.crdc_nurse_pct.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 96.2% of schools in 2021-22. Lowest: Cataño (80), Aguas Buenas (83.3), Ciales (83.3).
caveats: Schools report their own figures; the Office for Civil Rights does not audit them, and how a school counts an absence or a part-time staff member can differ.
Puerto Rico's staff items are missing in the 2017-18 collection, so the staff measures have 2021-22 only.
Any nurse counts, full- or part-time.
school_conditions.crdc_nurse_pct.source_detail: US Department of Education, Civil Rights Data Collection 2017-18 and 2021-22, public schools, via the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal; pooled by municipio

school_conditions.crdc_no_counselor_pct.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 51.5% of schools in 2021-22. Highest: Culebra (100), Trujillo Alto (90), Fajardo (80).
caveats: Schools report their own figures; the Office for Civil Rights does not audit them, and how a school counts an absence or a part-time staff member can differ.

school_conditions.crdc_absent_pct.plain: The share of students who missed 15 or more school days in the year, for any reason.
school_conditions.crdc_absent_pct.plain_es: La proporción de estudiantes que faltaron 15 días o más de clases en el año, por cualquier razón.
school_conditions.crdc_absent_pct.definition: Students absent 15 or more school days in the year, for any reason (excused or not), as a share of the students enrolled. Public schools that answered the Civil Rights Data Collection, placed in a municipio by the NCES school directory; the share is pooled over the schools that report both figures, never an average of school shares. school_conditions.crdc_absent_pct.method: school_conditions.py reads the all-students rows of the Civil Rights Data Collection for Puerto Rico's public schools, places each school in a municipio by its NCES id in the Common Core of Data directory of the same year, and pools: a municipio's share is the sum of its schools' numerators over the sum of their denominators, over the schools that report both. Negative codes (missing, not applicable, suppressed) are no value.
school_conditions.crdc_absent_pct.how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 8.9% in 2017-18 and 45.7% in 2021-22, the first year back in school buildings after the pandemic. Lowest in 2021-22: Guaynabo (11.2), Aibonito (12.7), San Juan (20); highest: Las Marías (83.2), Aguadilla (81), San Sebastián (77.6).
caveats: Schools report their own figures; the Office for Civil Rights does not audit them, and how a school counts an absence or a part-time staff member can differ.
Differences this large between neighbouring municipios may come partly from how each education region recorded absences: read neighbours together.
Check: the Annie E. Casey Foundation's 2024 KIDS COUNT release for Puerto Rico reports 48% of public school students chronically absent around 2022-23.
2017-18 was the school year of Hurricane María; schools that did not reopen are not in it.

proficiency.prof_math_pct.plain: The share of public school students tested in math who scored proficient or above on Puerto Rico's test.
proficiency.prof_math_pct.plain_es: La proporción de estudiantes de escuelas públicas evaluados en matemáticas que obtuvieron proficiente o más en la prueba de Puerto Rico.
proficiency.prof_math_pct.definition: The share of students tested in math who scored proficient or above on Puerto Rico's test. Public schools, all tested grades together, pooled over the students with a valid score; a small school's share comes as a range and its middle is used. Puerto Rico sets its own test (META-PR) and its own line for proficient: do not compare with a state. The newest school-level results a script can read end in 2018-19. The year is the school year that starts in it (2018 = 2018-19, tested in spring 2019).
proficiency.prof_math_pct.method: proficiency.py reads the all-students rows of the EDFacts assessment file for each school year (all grades together), places each school in a municipio by its NCES id in the Common Core of Data directory of the same year, and pools: a municipio's share is the sum over its schools of (share proficient x students tested) over the students tested. A small school's share comes as a range; its middle is used.
caveats: Puerto Rico sets its own test (META-PR) and its own line for proficient: do not compare these shares with a state's or with NAEP.
The newest results by school a script can read are 2018-19 (2019-20 was not tested); later island figures are in the Department of Education's reports, not by municipio.
Small schools report a range; from the bottom and the top of every range the island's 2018-19 figure is 29.3% to 31.1%.
About 265 schools closed after 2017-18, so 2018-19 covers fewer schools (836 against 1,090); a municipio's share can move because its students moved to other schools.
Check: the Department of Education's own 2018-19 results are 45.1% proficient in Spanish and 30.1% in math.
proficiency.prof_math_pct.source_detail: US Department of Education, EDFacts state assessment files, school years 2014-15 to 2018-19, via the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal; pooled by municipio
